Subject: Finlytics POC: success criteria, evaluation plan & weekly cadence

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed plan to keep the POC moving:

1) Agreed success criteria (candidate list)
- Latency: 95th percentile generation time <= 400ms for 512-token prompts (on dedicated_profile)
- Throughput: support >= 20 concurrent QPS for typical prompt mix
- Quality: mean relevance score >= 4.2/5 on your internal eval rubric for top-3 results
- Integration: embeddings-based rerank improves top-1 precision by >= 8% on your sample set

2) Evaluation plan
- Week 0 (this week): confirm success criteria, share sample data, set up minimal infra and credentials
- Week 1: data ingest + baseline runs (sample size: ~1k-10k rows)
- Week 2: model runs + metric collection + comparison against current baseline
- Week 3: run extended tests and finalize recommendations + handoff notes

3) Ownership
- Finlytics: Jordan (data access, evaluation rubric), Priya (product owner — success criteria sign-off)
- Redwood: Marcus (SE lead — ingestion + config), Marissa (program manager — timelines & rollout)

4) Immediate next steps (action items)
- Redwood: share POC template and success-criteria doc (attached) — DONE (see attachments)
- Finlytics: confirm sample dataset location and access method (S3 or secure upload) — ACTION: Jordan
- Finlytics: confirm which baseline metrics you want us to compute from the template (precision/recall, MRR, latency) — ACTION: Priya
- Redwood: schedule a 30-minute SE session to walk ingestion and sample config — PROPOSED: next Tue/Wed window

Attachments: Finlytics-POC-success-criteria.pdf, redwood-poc-template.xlsx

If this looks good I can send a calendar invite for the SE session after Jordan confirms the preferred time and access method.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks for the quick reply. Short answers to your questions and next steps on ingestion: 

- Format: CSV or Parquet both work. Parquet preferred for columnar performance but CSV is fine for initial runs.
- Minimal sample size: for stable signal on relevance metrics we recommend >= 1,000 labeled rows; 5k is a good target for early metric comparisons.
- Access: presigned S3 URLs are perfect. We do not need long-lived creds. If you prefer, we can also accept a secure temporary bucket with a time-limited role.

I've attached a small sample config to show the fields we read and sample transforms (data-ingest-sample-config.json). Steps I recommend: 
1) Drop a 5k sample CSV into a presigned S3 path (or share presigned link)
2) SE session (30 min) to validate schema and run first baseline pass
3) Iterate on transforms and metric collection

Available SE session slots (PDT): Tue 2026-07-07 10:00-10:30, Wed 2026-07-08 09:00-09:30, Wed 2026-07-08 15:00-15:30. Tell me which works and I will send an invite.

Attachment: data-ingest-sample-config.json

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the sample.

Best,
